Visual direction "The Chancery": the furniture of an old, calm royal chancery that has known peace for seventeen centuries. Panels are smooth dark oiled walnut, deliberately quiet with very little grain noise; borders are a single thin cast-bronze moulding with tiny gilt corner pieces; reading surfaces (the event body text and the focus description) are warm cream vellum with dark brown ink text; buttons are blackened iron plates with a fine gilt edge that brightens on hover and turns to a full gold rim when selected; icons sit in identical small round bronze bezels and are painted miniatures in a muted earthy palette. Palette: walnut brown, bronze, muted gold accent used sparingly, cream vellum, ink brown, with small enamel insets of verdigris green, amber and cinnabar red only for good, warning and danger. Restrained, orderly, high readability, strong hierarchy: titles in a refined serif, body text in a clean readable face. The screen shows, together and all at once: (1) across the very top, a slim resource top bar with a realm banner flag at the far left, small resource icons with short numbers, and a date plate at the far right; (2) directly beneath its left half, a narrower second strip, the "Aoaz bar", holding a "Realm" button, an age plate reading "4A 1748", a small dark-gathering meter with a value of 10, three small country meters with tiny icons, and one small round sigil button; (3) a large open national focus tree panel filling the left and centre of the screen: a titled window with a grid of about fourteen focus nodes (each a small square painted icon above a short title plate) joined by clean connector lines, one node highlighted as in progress with a thin progress bar, and a description panel at the bottom; (4) an event window on the right side, overlapping the map: a title, a painted landscape picture of a walled riverside town at dusk in a frame, three short paragraphs of body text, and two option buttons stacked beneath. Behind everything, a painted campaign map of a fantasy continent with coasts, rivers, forests and coloured realm borders is visible at the edges. Interface text is short, plain and legible English; there is no logo, no watermark and no signature. The interface is one consistent visual system: the same panel material, the same border, the same button shape and the same icon frame everywhere. The first reference image is one of this world's realm banners (use it as the realm flag in the top bar and as the craft and style reference for emblems); the second reference image shows this world's painted portrait style (do not show a portrait in this screen).
